endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: GV.MT-P7: Policies, processes, and procedures for receiving, tracking, and responding to complaints, concerns, and questions from individuals about organizational privacy practices are established and in place.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether a process for privacy complaints and questions about AI data processing changes how often individual concerns are heard or resolved. The recommendation rests on one framework endorsement from the CHAI Responsible AI Guide, which describes the practice without reporting outcome data.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence when no comparative or observational test exists. The single endorsement is expert consensus, which describes an expected practice but does not measure its effect.

The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide item GV.MT-P7 calls for policies to receive, track, and respond to individual complaints and questions about privacy practices. This is the only supplied source, and it is a voluntary framework. The materials provided do not link the item to any statute or rule, so its standing rests on framework adoption.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare organizations with and without a defined AI privacy complaint process and measure complaint volume, time to response, resolution rates, and patient trust. No supplied study documents how often AI-related privacy concerns currently go unheard, so the size of the hazard is also unmeasured.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether a complaint process reaches people who face language, literacy, or access barriers remains unknown, and health systems adopting it may need to collect their own data on who uses it.
